solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Thanks Mike, when confronting stormy North Sea, for hat

indicators.note: the first pieces stand facing the rest, so they come before it

parts.note: TA is informal British for thanks
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: a stormy sea is churned up, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the fodder letters, as written

explanation.surface: A man called Mike, about to face a rough North Sea crossing, is thanked for lending a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: TA and M come first, then the letters of NORTH SEA rearranged as OSHANTER, as 'stormy' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: A tam-o'-shanter is a round woollen Scottish bonnet with a bobble, a type of headwear.

clue.text: Giant bird on banks of Amazon

indicators.note: in a down clue the bird sits on top of what follows

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird

indicators.note: a river's banks are its two edges, so take the outside letters of the word

parts.note: the river's name supplies its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A huge bird is spotted perched on the banks of the Amazon river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Amazon' is a river here, so its banks are its first and last letters, A and N.
explanation.definitionFit: A titan is a person or being of enormous size or strength, after the Titans of Greek myth.

clue.text: Medical officer Una carries special tent for Italian peak

indicators.note: Una holds the other letters within her, as if carrying them

parts.note: a woman's name, taken as written

indicators.note: a special arrangement of letters means they are reordered

parts.note: the fodder letters, as written

explanation.surface: A doctor called Una lugs a special tent up an Italian mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: Una is taken literally as letters, not as a person; 'carries' puts the jumbled tent between her first letter and the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Etna is the active volcano on Sicily, the highest mountain in Italy south of the Alps.

clue.text: Wrongdoing outside public house by inscrutable person

indicators.note: the word for wrongdoing goes around the outside of the pub's letters

parts.note: a sin is a wrongdoing
PH is the map abbreviation for public house
X is the multiplication sign, read as 'by' (three by four)

explanation.surface: Misbehaviour outside a pub is witnessed by someone who gives nothing away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' gives X because dimensions are written with a multiplication sign, as in 3 x 4.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone enigmatic and unreadable is called a sphinx, after the riddling creature of Greek legend.

clue.text: Little weight in aluminium hand tool

indicators.note: the weight's letter is placed inside the chemical symbol

parts.note: Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium
W is the short form of weight, 'little' signalling the abbreviation

explanation.surface: A light aluminium tool for handwork is being described.
explanation.definitionFit: An awl is a small pointed instrument used by hand for piercing leather or wood.

clue.text: Row stifles stray dog

indicators.note: to stifle is to smother, so the row wraps around the other word

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
to err is to stray from the right path

explanation.surface: A noisy quarrel silences a wandering dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' reads as a quarrel, but it is a row of seats, a tier.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrier is a breed of small, lively dog originally used for hunting burrowing animals.

clue.text: Lost ciders, concerning newsman, found again

indicators.note: lost letters are scattered and out of their order, so they are rearranged

parts.note: the fodder letters, as written
over can mean concerning, as in a row over money
ED, short for editor, is the crossword newsman

explanation.surface: Some missing bottles of cider, according to a reporter, have turned up after all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concerning' as over is the sense in 'a dispute over pay'.
explanation.definitionFit: To rediscover something is to locate it once more after it was mislaid or forgotten.

clue.text: Cricket interval: one team munched Spam?

parts.note: lunch is the break taken during a day of a cricket match

indicators.note: munched food is chewed up, so these letters are broken and reshaped

parts.note: the fodder letters, as written

explanation.surface: During the lunch break at the cricket, one side ate tinned meat.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags Spam as just one brand standing for the whole category.
explanation.definitionFit: Spam is a well-known brand of tinned, processed pork, the classic example of this product.

clue.text: Lie high-class religious books near Old Testament book

indicators.note: the last book is placed next to the others

parts.note: U means upper-class, as in U and non-U
NT is the New Testament, a set of religious books
Ruth is a book of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A falsehood is told about posh scripture lying beside an Old Testament volume.
explanation.definitionFit: An untruth is a falsehood, a statement that is not true.

clue.text: Was guide around ancient city enticed?

indicators.note: the word for guided goes around the city's letters

parts.note: to have been a guide is to have led
Ur is the ancient Sumerian city in Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: Was the tour leader around the ruins of an old city tempted?
explanation.definitionFit: To be lured is to be tempted or drawn in by an attraction or bait.

clue.text: Position east of Charlie on European lake

indicators.note: in an across answer, east of means to the right of, so position comes last

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a stance is a position or posture

explanation.surface: A spot just to the east of a man called Charlie on a European lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Constance lies on the borders of Germany, Austria and Switzerland, fed by the Rhine.

clue.text: Instruction from Edward, head lowered in auction

parts.note: Ed is short for Edward

indicators.note: the word's first letter is moved further down, in this down clue

parts.note: the word as written, whose first letter shifts

explanation.surface: Edward gives guidance after his head drops during a sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head lowered' takes the A at the head of AUCTION and moves it down two places, giving UCATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Education is teaching or schooling, the giving of instruction.

clue.text: One's handling female's doubts

indicators.note: one's letters hold the female's letter, as hands hold something

parts.note: one is I, and 's is read as is, giving IS

explanation.surface: A person managing a woman's uncertainties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' is I plus 'is', so IS goes around F.
explanation.definitionFit: Ifs are uncertainties or reservations, as in 'no ifs or buts'.

clue.text: Substitute some workers at zoo

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A stand-in replaces some of the keepers at a zoo.
explanation.definitionFit: Ersatz describes an inferior imitation used in place of the real thing, a replacement.

clue.text: Relative in Spain agreed on jewellery

indicators.note: in a down clue the Spanish yes sits on top of the jewellery

parts.note: si is Spanish for yes, the word of agreement in Spain
bling is flashy jewellery

explanation.surface: A family member in Spain consents to some jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: A sibling is a brother or sister, a close family relation.

clue.text: Question, painting for example duck, size of paper

parts.note: painting is an example of art
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, so O

explanation.surface: A list of items is queried, ending in a size of paper.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a score of zero in cricket, giving O.
explanation.definitionFit: Quarto is a paper size made by folding a sheet twice to make four leaves.

clue.text: Jack to mimic tracks, jesting

parts.note: J is the card abbreviation for jack
to ape is to mimic
RY, short for railway, is a set of tracks

explanation.surface: A man named Jack copies someone's footprints in fun.
explanation.definitionFit: Japery is playful joking or larking about, from jape, a prank.

clue.text: On reflection, reject writer

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror is back to front, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to bin something is to throw it out

explanation.surface: After thinking it over, someone throws away a writer's manuscript.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On reflection' sounds like second thoughts, but it reverses BIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A nib is the point of a pen, the part that actually does the writing.

clue.text: Overwhelming rush of pain besetting naval invalid

indicators.note: to beset is to surround, so the pain's letters go around the rest

parts.note: an ache is a pain

indicators.note: an invalid arrangement is not correct, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the fodder letters, as written

explanation.surface: A wave of suffering besets a sailor who has been invalided out of service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invalid' reads as a sick person in the surface, but here it means not valid, signalling a rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: An avalanche is a sudden huge mass of snow falling down a slope, or by extension any overwhelming flood.

clue.text: Heard nicked criminal on trial here?

indicators.note: the word for nicked is spoken aloud to give a word sounding like it

parts.note: to be nicked is British slang for caught by police

explanation.surface: A heard rumour says the arrested crook will be on trial here.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech, caught and court sound alike; nicked is slang for arrested.
explanation.definitionFit: A court is the place where a criminal is tried, so this is a definition by example.

clue.text: Poet's private room almost west-facing

indicators.note: in an across clue, facing west means reading right to left, backwards
almost means the word stops short of its final letter

parts.note: a toilet is a private room

explanation.surface: A poet's study faces nearly westward.
explanation.walkthrough: TOILET loses its last letter ('almost') to give TOILE, which 'west-facing' reads backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: T. S. Eliot was the poet of The Waste Land; George Eliot was a novelist.

clue.text: Tasteless stuff, whichever way one looks

indicators.note: the word reads the same forwards and backwards, so looking either way gives it

parts.note: cheap tawdry goods; the definition doubles as the word to be read both ways

explanation.surface: Cheap tacky goods are everywhere one turns.
explanation.definitionFit: Tat is cheap, tawdry goods or rubbish, lacking good taste.

clue.text: Film in Europe initially engages bon vivant

indicators.note: the film's letters go inside the Europe letters

parts.note: a pic is a film

indicators.note: initially means take the opening letter

parts.note: the word whose first letter is used

explanation.surface: A movie shot in Europe is first to hire a lover of good living.
explanation.definitionFit: An epicure is a person who enjoys fine food and drink, a gourmet.

clue.text: Jersey might be so closely integrated

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a jersey, a knitted pullover, might be made with tight stitches
second meaning: bound together by strong relationships

explanation.walkthrough: Jersey looks like the Channel Island, which might be a close community; it is the jumper.
explanation.definitionFit: A tight-knit community is one whose members are closely bonded together, as stitches knitted tightly.
